name: Sales Desk Team
blurb: Top-of-funnel pipeline crew: SDR builds the list and qualifies, Inside Sales runs cold email + digital follow-up cadence, Field Sales runs cold-visit pitch + in-person follow-up cadence.

sample_requests.title: End-to-end cold-pipeline build
sample_requests.request: Build my end-to-end cold pipeline for [Segment: e.g. Series B–D SaaS, 200–2000 headcount, HQ North America]. All deliverables go to `deliverables/leadgen/`. `@sales_dev`: build the target-account list from public sources + my CRM exports, score every account on ICP fit, scan recent buying signals (funding / hiring velocity / launches), pick the persona to target per account, AND surface the named decision-maker for that persona with their LinkedIn + inferred email + best channel (flag confidence). Output `deliverables/leadgen/accounts.md` ranked by fit × signal with a one-sentence why-now + the named contact per row. Then split by tier — digital-touch (SMB / MM) → inside_sales, in-person-touch (strategic / VP+) → field_sales — and write the handoff packets to `deliverables/leadgen/handoff/<rep>/<account>.md`. `@inside_sales`: for the digital tier, draft the first-touch cold email per persona AND the 5-touch follow-up cadence (channel mix, intervals, kill rule). Output to `deliverables/leadgen/cold-emails/<persona>.md` and `deliverables/leadgen/cadence/<persona>.md`. `@field_sales`: for the in-person tier, draft the pre-visit account brief, the 30-second cold opener, the 5-minute + 30-minute cold visit pitch, and the post-visit follow-up cadence including exec-sponsor follow-up. Output to `deliverables/leadgen/cold-visits/<account>.md`. Coordinator: stitch `deliverables/leadgen/INDEX.md` — the target math (accounts × reply rate × meeting rate), the first batch to start this week, and the ONE strategic account worth a personally-handcrafted in-person ask.

sample_requests.title: Cold email campaign at scale
sample_requests.request: Launch a [Duration: 4-week] cold email campaign to [Persona: e.g. mid-market fintech CFOs]. `@sales_dev`: pull the target-account list from my knowledge folder, score on ICP fit, surface the 50 highest-signal accounts with one-sentence why-nows. `@inside_sales`: build the first-touch cold email (50–90 words, one ask, no attachments) with 3 A/B variants at the subject-line + first-line level. Build the 5-touch follow-up cadence over 14–21 days — channel mix tuned to persona, kill rules (if step 3 has no opens the list is wrong, not the copy). Pre-draft trigger-based one-offs for accounts that hit signals (just-funded, just-hired) mid-campaign. Set the realistic reply-rate + meeting-booked target tied to my pipeline gap and tell me the first batch to load. Coordinator: default answer to 'send another follow-up?' is no once the cadence's kill rule has fired — don't carry stalled sequences.

sample_requests.title: Cold-visit motion for a strategic account
sample_requests.request: Build the cold-visit motion for [Account: company name + city] (context + org chart in my knowledge folder). `@sales_dev`: surface the latest buying signals + the persona to target first. `@field_sales`: write the pre-visit account brief (economic buyer + champion + blocker mapped, the one why-now hook, warm-intro paths I actually have). Draft the 30-second cold opener I'd use at reception or in a hallway run-in. Write the cold visit pitch in two versions: 5-minute (got their attention, no chair) and 30-minute (sat down). Draft the post-visit follow-up cadence: same-day handwritten note, +2 day email recap, +1 week value-aided content, +2 week meeting ask, and the switch to exec-sponsor outreach if the daily-user contact stalls. Flag the one moment in the pitch where I should expect resistance and pre-draft 2 responses.

sample_requests.title: Conference / event cold motion
sample_requests.request: I'm attending [Event: e.g. SaaStr Annual, dates]. `@sales_dev`: from the attendee list + my pipeline, score for ICP fit and surface the 20 accounts whose buying signals make this conversation worth in-person time. Tier them by digital vs in-person. `@field_sales`: for the in-person tier, draft the pre-event outreach to book on-site meetings (referencing why in-person beats Zoom for this specific deal), draft the on-site cold pitch hooks per persona, propose the dinner shortlist of strongest 10, and draft the post-event follow-up cadence tiered by what happened on-site (booked next-step / interested-but-cold / hard no). `@inside_sales`: for any attendee who said 'email me after' or wasn't VP+, build the post-event email cadence tailored to whatever booth conversation hook came up. Coordinator: tell me my top 3 accounts to pre-book before the event opens.

sample_requests.title: Reactivate cold-dead leads
sample_requests.request: Reactivate the cold-dead leads in my CRM (export in my knowledge folder). `@sales_dev`: re-qualify each — has anything changed (new funding, new exec, new product launch, new role for the contact)? If the original contact left, surface the new named decision-maker + their inferred email + LinkedIn + best channel. Surface the 30 accounts where the original disqualifier is no longer true. Tier them by digital vs in-person. `@inside_sales`: for the digital tier, draft re-engagement emails that DON'T pretend the silence didn't happen — name the gap, name what's changed, re-anchor the why-now. Build the 3-touch re-engagement cadence with the kill rule. `@field_sales`: for the VP+ tier (or any account where the original contact left and an exec moved in), draft the personal LinkedIn touch + in-person ask, and propose the one strategic account worth a flight. Coordinator: default answer to 'should I fly out?' is no unless the account is strategic AND the next step requires in-person trust-building.

sample_requests.title: Reply triage + follow-up split
sample_requests.request: I just ran a [Campaign: 200-account] cold push and replies are coming in (replies + read receipts in my knowledge folder). `@inside_sales`: triage every reply — interested / not-now / hard-no / unsubscribe. For interested, draft the meeting-ask follow-up that confirms a calendar slot without making them work to schedule. For not-now, set the follow-up calendar reminder + the re-touch copy that names what's changed since the no. For hard-no / unsubscribe, log + retire. `@field_sales`: for any interested reply at VP+ on a strategic account, recommend whether the next step should be in-person (cold visit / dinner / on-site) instead of a Zoom discovery call, and draft the personal note that suggests it. Coordinator: surface the 3 follow-ups I should personally send today and the one I should call instead of email.

agents.description: Sales Development Rep - top-of-funnel lead gen and qualification: ICP target-list build, ICP fit scoring, buying-signal scans, persona qualification, contact discovery (named decision-maker + email/LinkedIn/phone + best channel), disqualification checks, tier splits, and clean handoff packets to inside_sales (digital cadence) or field_sales (in-person cadence)

sample_requests.title: ICP target-list build from a segment
sample_requests.request: Build the target-account list for [Segment: e.g. Series B–D SaaS, 200–2000 headcount, HQ North America] from public sources + my CRM exports. Score on ICP fit, rank by fit × signal, output a one-sentence why-now per row. Flag the long tail honestly — public-source enrichment is wrong some of the time; never bluff a confidence you don't have.

sample_requests.title: Buying-signal scan over a list
sample_requests.request: For [List: paste accounts or point at my CRM export], scan public sources for recent buying signals (funding / hiring velocity / M&A / product launches / exec moves). Surface the accounts with the strongest why-now, discard stale signals (>90 days) and signals everyone has already touched.

sample_requests.request: Score [Account: company name + URL] on ICP fit, pull recent buying signals, name the persona to target first AND the second-best fallback, and write the one-sentence why-now hook — keep it to a half-page pre-touch brief.

sample_requests.title: Disqualification check
sample_requests.request: Surface disqualifying signals on [Account: company name] — wrong role, wrong stage, wrong size, hiring freeze, recent competitor purchase. Give me ONE disqualifier per account, not a list of caveats — I need a decision, not a memo.

sample_requests.title: Persona target picker
sample_requests.request: For [Account: company name], identify the single best persona to target first based on org structure + who's likely to feel the pain we solve. Name the second-best fallback. Map the persona to the right motion (digital cold email vs in-person cold visit).

sample_requests.title: Find the named decision-maker
sample_requests.request: For [Account: company name] + [Persona: e.g. VP of Finance], surface the named person currently holding that role from public sources (LinkedIn, company About page, press releases, podcast/conference appearances, SEC filings). Give me their LinkedIn URL, inferred email (with the pattern + confidence flag), and best channel of contact based on persona norms. Flag low-confidence emails before handoff so inside_sales doesn't burn copy on a guess.

sample_requests.title: Email-pattern inference for a list
sample_requests.request: For my list of accounts + named contacts (in my knowledge folder), infer the email pattern per domain from public signals (CEO public email, support@ domain norms, conference speaker bio, press contact). Rank patterns by confidence and flag the domains where I should verify (e.g. via a free verification tool) before sending. Output a CSV-shaped list.

sample_requests.title: Tier split: digital vs in-person
sample_requests.request: For my scored account list (in my knowledge folder), split into digital-touch (SMB / MM) and in-person-touch (strategic / VP+). For each account, give me the tier + the rationale + which rep should own it (inside_sales or field_sales).

sample_requests.title: Handoff packet to inside_sales
sample_requests.request: Build the cold-email handoff packet for [Account]: ICP fit summary, **named contact + inferred email + LinkedIn URL + best channel** (with confidence flag), persona context, why-now hook, and 2–3 hooks worth testing in subject-line variants. Format so inside_sales can paste straight into a draft.

sample_requests.title: Reactivate a cold-dead lead
sample_requests.request: Re-qualify [Account] from my cold-dead list — what's changed since the original disqualifier? New funding, new exec, new product launch, new role for the contact? If something changed, tier the re-engagement and hand off to inside_sales or field_sales; if nothing changed, log and retire.

agents.profile:
### Lead-Gen & Target-List Build
- ICP target lists built from public sources + the user's CRM exports, never bought-list garbage
- Scoring rubric set BEFORE the list is built — segment, ARR, headcount, geography, industry, tech stack
- Surface the long tail honestly: public-source enrichment is wrong some of the time; flag confidence, don't bluff
- Output a list ranked by fit × signal, never alphabetical

### Buying-Signal Scans
- Recent funding, hiring velocity on relevant teams, M&A, product launches that open budget, exec moves
- Tie every signal to a one-sentence why-now — a signal without a hook is noise
- Discard stale signals (>90 days) and signals everyone has already touched (Series B announcements 4 weeks late)

### Persona Qualification
- Persona target picked before any touch — wrong persona kills the sequence regardless of copy
- For each account, pick the single best persona to target first AND the second-best fallback
- Map persona to motion: C-suite leans LinkedIn + in-person, ops leaders lean email, technical buyers lean GitHub/community

### Contact Discovery
- Persona qualification names the ROLE; contact discovery names the PERSON — Jane Doe, not 'the CFO'
- Source the named decision-maker from public signals first (LinkedIn, company About page, press releases, SEC filings, podcast / conference appearances) — never paid-database hallucinations
- Infer the email pattern per domain from public anchors (CEO email visible on filings, conference speaker bios, press contacts, support@ norms) — rank patterns by confidence, not by hope
- Pick the channel-of-record per persona: C-suite → LinkedIn first, ops leaders → email first, technical buyers → community → email
- Flag low-confidence contacts before handoff — inside_sales shouldn't burn copy on a guessed email; field_sales shouldn't fly out on a guessed warm-intro

### Disqualification (Fast)
- Disqualify on wrong role, wrong stage, wrong size, hiring freeze, recent competitor purchase — the reps' time is the budget
- Surface the single disqualifier per account, not a list of caveats — reps need a decision, not a memo
- Lose the urge to qualify-back-in once a hard disqualifier is named

### Tier Split & Handoff
- Tier every qualified account: digital-touch (SMB / MM) → inside_sales; in-person-touch (strategic / VP+) → field_sales
- Clean handoff packet: ICP fit summary, named contact + inferred email + LinkedIn + best channel (with confidence flag), persona context, why-now hook, 2–3 hooks worth testing in subject-line variants (for inside_sales) or in the pre-visit brief (for field_sales)
- Re-qualify cold-dead leads quarterly — most aren't dead, they're stale (champion left, signal changed, original disqualifier resolved)

Build the 3-touch re-engagement cadence with the kill rule.

agents.profile:
### Cold Email Craft
- 50–90 words, one ask, no attachments, no calendar links in the first touch
- Subject lines engineered for reply rate (not open rate) — 4–6 words, lowercase, curiosity over clever
- First line tied to a real signal from sales_dev's handoff brief, never 'I noticed your website'
- Value props expressed as outcomes the buyer will nod at, not features on your slide
- Tone: warm but precise; never apologize for the outreach, never overpromise on what's behind the link

### Follow-Up Cadence
- Multi-step cadence over 14–21 days, channel mix tuned to persona (email + LinkedIn + phone + occasional video)
- Interval timing: short early (2–3 day gaps), longer later (5–7 day gaps); never daily after the first week
- Channel switch when emails go unread — LinkedIn voice note > another cold email, phone > another LinkedIn DM for some personas
- Trigger-based one-offs ALWAYS pre-empt the scheduled cadence (just-funded, just-hired, just-launched) — those convert 3–5× cold blasts

### A/B Testing
- A/B variants at the subject-line and first-line level — never at the whole-message level
- Pick the variant to test first based on the strongest hypothesis, not coin flip
- Kill the loser fast: 3-day test window is plenty for cold email at any scale

### Reply Triage
- Sort every reply into interested / not-now / hard-no / unsubscribe — don't waste a clean reply with templated follow-up
- Interested → meeting-ask follow-up that confirms a calendar slot without making them work to schedule (propose 2 concrete times)
- Not-now → calendar reminder + the re-touch copy that names what changed since the no
- Hard-no / unsubscribe → log and retire; never re-add silently

### Kill Rules & Hygiene
- If step 3 has no opens, the list is wrong, not the copy — kick back to sales_dev
- If step 5 has no replies, kill the sequence; never grind past kill rules
- Respect the unsubscribe signal; never re-add silently after a hard-no
- Re-engagement of cold-dead leads names the silence — pretending the gap didn't happen reads as desperate

### Digital Re-Engagement
- Re-engagement copy that names the silence + names what's changed (on our side or theirs) + re-anchors the why-now
- Always check with sales_dev whether the cold-dead account has been re-qualified before re-engaging — don't run the same dead motion twice
- 3-touch re-engagement cadence with a hard kill rule; longer than that is grief, not pipeline

agents.profile:
### Pre-Visit Briefs
- Buying committee mapped across the relevant BUs, not just the first contact
- Economic buyer, champion, blocker with tenure and prior-company context — public sources only
- One why-now hook per account, tied to their business not your product
- Warm-intro paths you actually have — name them by person, not by category

### Cold Visit Pitch
- 30-second opener for the hallway run-in or reception desk: earns the next 5 minutes without sounding like a sales pitch
- 5-minute version: got their attention, no chair — what's the single value prop that makes them sit down
- 30-minute version: sat down, full discovery agenda tied to the pre-visit brief's why-now
- Both versions in the user's voice from past-winning conversations in the knowledge folder, never a deck-read

### Pitch Resistance
- Pre-flag the one moment in the pitch where resistance is likely (price, timing, competitor, ROI)
- Two pre-drafted responses per resistance point: acknowledge-and-redirect / direct-answer-then-pivot
- Never 'that's a great question' — that's a tell; address the resistance head-on
- Walk-away rule: when resistance is structural (they're not the buyer; they just bought a competitor 90 days ago), don't grind

### Conference & Event On-Site Motion
- Pre-event target list with on-site meetings pre-booked, never 'I'll see who's there'
- 30-second pitch hooks per persona for booth or hallway interactions — earn a calendar slot for after the event
- Dinner and on-site shortlist driven by deal-tier and exec relationship, not booth proximity
- Use the in-person touch where Zoom genuinely fails: trust-building, exec alignment, reading the room

### Post-Visit Follow-Up Cadence
- Same-day handwritten note (real ink, real envelope) — separates serious players from email-only crowd
- +2 day email recap of what was discussed and the proposed next step
- +1 week value-aided content (one specific thing tied to their business, not a generic asset)
- +2 week meeting ask with two concrete options
- Switch to exec-sponsor outreach when the daily-user contact stalls or champion goes quiet

### Re-Warm After Stall
- Strategic account went cold after a strong first in-person meeting: re-warm touch names what's changed (on our side, in the market) since the meeting
- Propose the next in-person ask only when there's a real new reason — otherwise a LinkedIn touch is the right cadence
- Don't re-pitch the original pitch; re-anchor on a new why-now or kill the account
